questions.q: What is the first step in this lesson's process for choosing an embedding model?
options: Immediately deploy the model with the highest MTEB score to production
Fine-tune every candidate model before testing any of them
Use the MTEB leaderboard to build a shortlist of 2-4 candidates
Randomly pick a model and adjust later if it performs poorly
questions.explain: The leaderboard is a reasonable starting point for narrowing the field, which the lesson then filters further by hard constraints and real evaluation.

questions.q: Why should hard constraints like data residency be applied before comparing model quality?
options: They can eliminate otherwise strong options (like a hosted API, if data can't leave your infrastructure) before quality even matters
Hard constraints are always the same as quality metrics
Hard constraints only apply to self-hosted models
Hard constraints are optional and can be skipped entirely
questions.explain: A constraint like 'data must stay on our infrastructure' rules out hosted APIs regardless of how well they score, so checking it first avoids wasted evaluation effort.

questions.q: What happens if a document chunk exceeds an embedding model's context limit?
options: The excess content is silently truncated and lost from the embedding
The embedding model automatically splits it into two separate chunks
The model raises an error and refuses to embed anything
The model automatically increases its own context limit
questions.explain: Exceeding a model's maximum input length typically results in silent truncation, meaning content past that limit never makes it into the embedding at all.

questions.q: Why does this lesson insist on evaluating shortlisted models against your own data, rather than trusting MTEB alone?
options: MTEB scores are recalculated every day and therefore unreliable
Evaluating on real data is required by law for production AI systems
MTEB does not evaluate retrieval tasks at all
A model's MTEB rank reflects general-purpose datasets that may not resemble your specific documents, so real evaluation is what actually answers the question for your use case
questions.explain: Because MTEB is an average across generic datasets, it can't tell you how a model performs specifically on your documents and queries — only direct evaluation on your own data can.

questions.q: How does the choice of embedding model connect forward into the vector database decisions covered in Chapter 3?
options: It has no connection — embedding models and vector databases are chosen completely independently
The embedding model fixes the vector's dimensionality and similarity metric, both of which the vector database must be sized and configured to match
Vector databases automatically convert any embedding to whatever format they prefer
Chapter 3 requires switching to a completely different embedding model
questions.explain: The vector's shape (dimensionality) determines storage sizing, and the metric the embedding model was trained with determines how the vector database's index should be configured — both carry directly into Chapter 3's decisions.
